questions.question: How does garbage collection work in JavaScript? Explain mark-and-sweep.
questions.title: JavaScript Garbage Collection — Mark-and-Sweep Explained
questions.direct_answer:
How does garbage collection work in JavaScript? Explain mark-and-sweep.

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Reachability from GC roots, mark-and-sweep algorithm, generational GC in V8 (young/old), incremental/concurrent marking.

**Classic weak answer:** Thinking setting a variable to null always frees memory — only if no other references exist; GC decides when to collect.

**Senior finish:** Mention V8's Orinoco GC, hidden classes, major vs minor GC, and WeakMap/WeakRef for leak-free caches.

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Thinking setting a variable to null always frees memory — only if no other references exist; GC decides when to collect
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Mention V8's Orinoco GC, hidden classes, major vs minor GC, and WeakMap/WeakRef for leak-free caches

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **JavaScript Garbage Collection — Mark-and-Sweep Explained** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** How does garbage collection work in JavaScript? Explain mark-and-sweep.

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **Reachability from GC roots, mark-and-sweep algorithm, generational GC in V8 (young/old), incremental/concurrent marking**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Thinking setting a variable to null always frees memory — only if no other references exist; GC decides when to collect**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Mention V8's Orinoco GC, hidden classes, major vs minor GC, and WeakMap/WeakRef for leak-free caches**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** Reachability from GC roots, mark-and-sweep algorithm, generational GC in V8 (young/old), incremental/concurrent marking
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **thinking setting a variable to null always frees memory — only if no other references exist; GC decides when to collect** and what you do instead.

questions.question: What are common memory-leak patterns in JavaScript? How do you detect and fix them?
questions.title: Common JavaScript Memory Leaks — Detached DOM, Timers, Closures
questions.direct_answer:
What are common memory-leak patterns in JavaScript? How do you detect and fix them?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the type checker, emit pipeline, and how types line up with runtime JS), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** Detached DOM references, forgotten timers/intervals, event listeners, global variables, closures holding large data, out-of-view React refs.

**Classic weak answer:** Assuming the browser cleans up intervals and event listeners automatically — it doesn't; you must clear/remove them explicitly.

**Senior finish:** Walk a Chrome DevTools Memory-tab workflow (heap snapshot, allocation timeline, retainers), and name common React patterns (useEffect cleanup, AbortController).

interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Assuming the browser cleans up intervals and event listeners automatically — it doesn't; you must clear/remove them explicitly
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Walk a Chrome DevTools Memory-tab workflow (heap snapshot, allocation timeline, retainers), and name common React patterns (useEffect cleanup, AbortController)
